paraphrase: Argues a retry is a second action, not recovery. Reports a small deterministic model of 10,000 tool calls where 2,674 responses were deliberately ambiguous; retrying without an idempotency key produced 12,674 effects (26.74% more than intended), while an idempotency key scoped to the intended action produced exactly 10,000. The quantitative values are author-claimed simulation results, not independently verified.

claims.text: A retry is a second action. A timeout is not a rollback.
claims.notes: Claimed failure mode: ambiguous completion + retry as a new effect

claims.text: In a deterministic model of an agent calling a state-changing tool 10,000 times with 2,674 deliberately ambiguous responses, retrying without an idempotency key produced 12,674 effects from 10,000 intended requests: 26.74% more writes, messages, purchases, or permission changes than the plan contained
claims.notes: Author-claimed simulation result; not empirically verified

claims.text: With an idempotency key scoped to the intended action, the model produced exactly 10,000 effects
claims.notes: Author-claimed simulation result; proposed control measure

claims.text: A retry after a lost response can send a duplicate email, create two tickets, or transfer value twice, and the agent's trace can look perfectly reasonable because it saw no success, so it tried again
claims.notes: Claimed failure mode: duplicate effects at external interfaces

evaluation.notes: Global discovery candidate c390cb33; simulation values author-claimed, unchecked
